background_rationale: Trained as an auditor and partner at Price Waterhouse, he held finance roles at PepsiCo and served as Delta's controller and CFO before becoming president and CEO.

notable.summary: After the CrowdStrike software outage triggered days of mass cancellations at Delta, which the airline put at about $500 million in losses, Bastian drew criticism for traveling to the Paris Olympics during the disruption.
After a Delta aircraft crashed at Toronto Pearson International Airport, Bastian announced $30,000 in compensation for each passenger plus coverage of medical expenses.
On Delta's first-quarter earnings call, Bastian said the airline would defer any aircraft deliveries subject to tariffs rather than pay them.

personal_story.hook: The oldest of nine kids, Ed Bastian didn't fly until 25; he now runs Delta.
personal_story.summary: Bastian grew up in Poughkeepsie, New York, the oldest of nine children of a dentist who practiced from the family home, with his mother as the dental assistant. He worked blue-collar jobs, earned an accounting degree from St. Bonaventure, and as a young Price Waterhouse auditor uncovered $50 million in phony revenue at J. Walter Thompson, helping him make partner at 31. After years in finance at PepsiCo, he joined Delta as controller in 1998, then quit in protest during the post-9/11 crisis, saying management decisions did not match the company's values or his own. About six months later he returned as CFO at half the salary to steer Delta through bankruptcy, then rose to president in 2007 and CEO in 2016.
